items.body: The first Wandelweiser release by composer Paul Beaudoin, bright shining light, is now available as a digital album download at Bandcamp. Consisting of the composer’s complete organ works to 2025, the five tracks on this album are performed by Carson Cooman, organist at Memorial Church, Harvard University. Paul Beaudoin is a composer, educator and interdisciplinary artist, born in Hialeah, Florida. He studied at the New England Conservatory of Music and received a PhD in Music Theory from Brandeis University. His music has been performed by the Lydian String Quartet, the Buffalo Quartet and as part of the Piano Spheres series in Los Angeles. In 2015 Paul was awarded a Fulbright Scholarship that brought him to Estonia where he continues to compose and write.Paul Beaudoin writes about bright shining light: “This is not a typical organ recital album. The music moves between fragile resonance, sustained intensity, harmonic pressure, brightness, stillness, and force.” bright shining light is an hour of inspiring organ music that employs all the power of that instrument to draw the listener into a state of contemplation and reflection. The title track of the album opens with a deep, full chord that builds upwards from the lowest registers of the pipe organ. This is a powerful, weighty sound much like the initial sensation of seeing a bright shining light. The notes are all sustained tones, with no perceptible rhythm or beat. The tones in the chord are changing pitch at what seems a glacial pace, but the sound is never static. The chord crowds itself together, suggesting the image of a great cathedral nave reaching ever upwards. As the piece proceeds, higher tones are heard above the bass register, thinning out the sound. The overall feeling becomes more reserved and somber as the piece winds down to its conclusion. The liner notes state that “bright shining light was composed in memory of Alexei Navalny and all those who fight oppression.” There is a definite sense of quiet strength and unyielding resistance here, aided by the perceptive playing of Carson Cooman. The power and intensity of the pipe organ is fully exploited, even without the presence of keyboard pyrotechnics. bright shining light presents a rewarding sonic experience that is both artistically inspiring and resolutely defiant in its realization.et caecitas eorum lacrimas eis efficiet, the second track, translates as “and their blindness shall make them weep.” The composer writes that the piece “…captures the tension between certainty and doubt, inviting listeners to consider the impact of their convictions.” This track continues to exploit the full resources of the organ, opening with a bold, sustained tone in the middle register that is soon joined by more notes to form a chord of intensity and power. These pitches are sustained and vary only slightly once established. At 1:00, a bass pedal tone is added, providing a solid foundation. The texture of the chords thin and thicken as the piece proceeds, reflecting certainty replaced by doubt. At times, the feeling is majestic but without the need for overwhelming the listener with raw power. A high flute tone quietly hangs in the air at the finish accompanied by a soft bass tone that provides a soft landing for this impressive piece. The longest track of the album, at over 23 minutes, is notes of union and longing. This opens with a very low sustained tone, soon joined by a new notes in the middle register. More notes follow to form a lovely chord whose pitches slowly change to create a series of warm and welcoming colors. The tempo is unhurried and the tones are without beat or pulse. At 2:40 some dissonance creeps in as the texture above thins and the low tone in the bass drops out adding an anxious feel. After a short pause, a new chord is formed in the middle to upper registers. The addition of a strong bass tone adds a warm foundation that suggests union after longing. These feelings of separation and union flow in and out as the dissonance in the chords come and go. The chord textures change with and without the bass, while the higher registers dominate to yield a variety of emotional colors. The coming and going of the strong bass tone always decisively shifts the mood to one of warmth and welcoming. When slightly dissonant, the tones in the higher register effectively suggest alienation and longing. Paul Beaudoin writes that “In this piece, my intention was to convey the emotions of union and longing through a delicate interplay of voice-leading and harmony, creating a space for introspection.” The tempo throughout the piece is always slow and deliberate, producing a sense of dignity and gravitas. A very high sustained tone at 14:45 suggests completion, even as the other notes in the chord are searching for resolution. A sense of the familiar is heard in the transparency and consonance of the upper register chords as the piece glides to a peaceful finish. notes of union and longing is a graceful, contemplative piece that gently invites the listener into quiet reflection.stillness emerging, track 4, is written for organ and fixed electronic media. The liner notes explain that “…the fixed electronic soundfield serves as a sonic canvas, providing a rich and immersive backdrop against which the organist paints with musical phrases.” This opens with a soft, low rumbling followed by higher tones that soon join in. As in the rest of the album, these are dense chords that are comprised of sustained tones that slowly change in pitch. The higher tones are most prominent, but very soft with a hospitable feel. Bass pedal tones continue to rumble below, but are almost inaudible. There is a mystical feeling to all of this. As the piece continues, the dynamics in upper notes seem to be slowly increasing, as if emerging. The electronic sounds and the organ blend seamlessly; it is hard to hear where one leaves off or the other begins. A whoosh of wind and a low, recurring scratching in the bass add to the intrigue. The entire piece is quietly serene and the dynamic contrasts are achieved by smooth variations in the texture. stillness emerging ends as it began – quietly. The final track of the album is grace abounding and this opens with a soft pedal tone in the bass. Airy flute tones are heard above in a simple melody and the feeling is both meditative and comforting. Paul Beaudoin writes that “grace abounding explores the concept of grace not as a static, singular experience but as an ever-present force that reaches beyond us, continually flowing and overflowing.” Accordingly, the pedal tone in the bass weaves in and out of the texture with the melody in the upper registers always in the foreground. A sustained, higher pitch often soars above, brightly underlining the melody. At the finish, a resolving chord is heard in the lower registers. grace abounding artfully portrays a process that is constantly at work in our lives, despite our human failings. bright shining light invokes all the majesty of a large pipe organ but expresses that power in harmonic nuance and textural subtlety, drawing the listener into deep reflection as well as into an emotional reaction. Those who appreciate the grand sounds of the cathedral organ will not be disappointed, but should be prepared to find themselves thinking meditatively about this music as well as experiencing its exhilaration.bright shining light is available for digital download at Bandcamp. items.body: Ten years is a long time to leave a dancefloor waiting. Buraka Som Sistema have spent most of that decade apart, and on Friday 7 August they walk back onto a UK stage at South London Miniteca: a free, all-day celebration of the Latin American and Afro-Luso communities of South London, out in the open in Burgess Park. Pulling the Main Stage together from midday are ¡Como No!, the capital’s leading Latin promoter since the 1980s and the outfit behind La Linea. The Lisbon crew spent the late 2000s welding Angolan kuduro to European club music, a sound that reached far past Portugal on tracks like “Sound of Kuduro“, made with M.I.A., “Hangover (BaBaBa)“, and “Kalemba (Wegue Wegue)“. Their 2008 album Black Diamond set the template, and two more followed, Komba in 2011 and Buraka in 2014. Years of touring took them from Caracas to Paris, India and Luanda, filmed across those cities in Off the Beaten Track, with an MTV Europe Music Award picked up along the way. They stepped away in 2016 and scattered into solo work, with Branko steering the Enchufada label and Kalaf turning to writing and cultural work. This summer they regrouped for the label’s twentieth anniversary and released “Puro Mambo”, an Angolan-slang title and their first new music in twelve years, alongside a run of festival dates and the first vinyl pressing of their full catalogue. Blaya, whose voice became part of the group’s identity as it grew, is back out front. Where Buraka bent kuduro, Son Rompe Pera bend cumbia, running their marimbas through punk. The second headliners of the festival, the Gama brothers grew up playing the wooden keys at weddings and quinceañeras in Naucalpan, on the edge of Mexico City, alongside their father Batuco; as teenagers they swapped it for punk, then dragged the marimba back with all that noise attached. After Batuco’s death, an invitation from Chilean cumbia veterans Chico Trujillo in 2017 pulled them back to music, and the cumbia punk they play now tips traditional Mexican and pan-Latin songs into garage, ska and surf. A new album, Marimbazos de Oro, follows in September on Mixto Records, produced by the Black Pumas’ Adrian Quesada, with lead single “Nada Que Hacer”. Live, they pull cumbia dancers and moshers to the same marimba. If Lisbon and Mexico City set the day’s coordinates, the rest of the Main Stage answers from London itself. Pianist Eliane Correa built Las Salseras here as the UK’s first all-female salsa orchestra, ten players drawn from across Latin America and the UK. Cuban percussionists Madelin Espinosa and Lidia María Madruga anchor the rhythm section with Argentine multi-percussionist Gala Celia, and Afro-Latin singer Juanita Euka takes the front, a voice that has carried this music at the Barbican and Glastonbury. Between them they have backed Los Van Van’s Mayito Rivera and Jimmy Bosch and tour with Hans Zimmer and Jessie Ware. Correa, who counts herself as much Argentinian and European as Cuban, is blunt about the all-women line-up, “We are not tokens”, a counterweight to the male bands salsa has run on for most of its life. They mark Celia Cruz’s centenary with “La Vida es un Carnaval” and “Quimbara”, alongside Tito Puente’s “Oye Cómo Va” and deeper cuts from the Queen of Salsa’s catalogue. Latinas of London brings a second all-women line-up to the stage, with Allexa Nava crossing over from the salsa orchestra. Desta French runs it on one rule, Latinas backing Latinas, no one above anyone else. A Camden singer of Colombian and Italian parentage, she was the first UK Latin artist played on BBC Radio with an all-Spanish-language song, back in 2020; she writes across jazz, hip-hop and cumbia, and her nights at the Jazz Café have turned into full-room Selena singalongs. Alongside Nava she brings Xativa, whose folk-leaning songs draw on Spanish and Ecuadorian roots. A second stage, Bailoteo, is given over to Latin American sound system culture, run by Bushbby, who started the Candelita night with Desta French. London-born with Colombian roots, she plays cumbia, champeta, reggaetón and dembow off the systems she grew up around. DJ Sueño joins her with the cumbiatón he sharpened in Rosa Pistola’s Mexico City circle, Sabor a Mi runs from guaguancó through cumbia to afro-house on vinyl, and Movimientos resident Amancai, who grew up in Cartagena, threads Colombian Caribbean sounds through afrobeats. Between sets there are children’s sports, yoga and stretching sessions, DJ workshops and food from across the Latin and Lusophone world, open to every age.   South London Miniteca runs from 12pm at Burgess Park on 07/08 Entry is free, though tickets should be booked ahead. Full details and booking are on Dice   https://rhythmpassport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AQN_OqLUuwDQPUykEz7IUF2r_or88TQL8tbWQhzbPiELPxiEZiU8w35P2el5YbcOlFqi1_i3NMCPm9nlnYpo5A10H8oyG-kr4Jq8Pl4.mp4 The post Event Preview: South London Miniteca @ Burgess Park (London; Friday, 7th August 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa厂牌第44号发行，收录贝宁歌手Antoine Dougbé与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo de Cotonou在1977至1982年间的合作录音。Dougbé被称为'魔鬼首相'，是一位伏都教实践者，其音乐以拍击大腿产生的Cavacha节奏为基础，该节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节奏中提炼，后广泛传播于中非流行音乐。专辑横跨70年代末至80年代初，吉他带有塑料质感，合成器开始出现，古巴son与刚果rumba的影响清晰可闻。《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺底，吉他干涩紧绷，在稳定的踩镲节奏上展开。《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则更直接地呈现古巴风格，以牛铃与鼻音人声呼应。Dougbé录制约三张专辑和若干单曲，产量不多但密度集中，展现了贝宁流行音乐中伏都传统与非洲古巴融合的具体形态。

items._cn_summary: 这张作品由作曲家大卫·祖宾斯基创作，是Prism萨克斯四重奏"释放你的内在作曲家"系列企划的一部分。2025年11月在费城自由图书馆现场演出时，四重奏邀请了人声歌手厄休拉·拉克、打击乐手泰肖恩·索雷以及小提琴家卡洛斯·圣地亚哥共同参与编排与演奏，形成古典室内乐编制与爵士即兴人声及实验打击乐的跨界碰撞。整首作品时长不到四分钟，从粗粝的声响迅速转入抒情段落再折返，兼具控制力与爆发力。评论来自RootsWorld杂志编辑的简短推荐，指出这是了解Prism四重奏跨界美学的良好切入点。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 本张专辑记录了Dr. John于1999年在德国莱茵河畔洛雷莱露天剧场的现场演出，乐队由吉他手Bobby Broom、贝斯手David Barard与鼓手Herman Ernest组成，编制紧凑而富有权威感。整场演出以新奥尔良狂欢节主题贯穿，混编新奥尔良经典曲目与个人代表作。开场以半唱半诵的'Iko, Iko'引入社区参与的狂欢节队列氛围，'Qualified'展现直白的自信宣言，而'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'则将funknology、gris-gris草药学与巫毒咒语意象融合，伴以丛林式呐喊、诡异滑哨与迷幻吉他独奏。专辑还收录'Sweet Home New Orleans''Goin' Back to New Orleans'等体现故乡情结的作品，并以Duke Ellington的'I'm Gonna Go Fishin''致敬影响，以Earl King的'Big Chief'收束于另一首狂欢节烈曲。整体呈现出跨越语言与文化障碍的音乐感染力。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威音乐家组成的三重奏录制，以挪威Taragot厂牌发行。三位音乐家均有跨界探索的背景，将斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材重新诠释，呈现出室内乐般的亲密对话感，而非可供舞蹈伴奏的常规演绎。他们刻意挖掘舞曲表层之下的暗流与神秘意味，开篇选用挪威塞特斯达尔山谷的传说主题曲"Fossgrimen"便暗示了这种倾向——水妖传说与小提琴被视为"魔鬼乐器"的文化记忆被纳入音乐叙事。在一首瑞典Polska中，旋律以齐奏引入后迅速瓦解、碎裂、戛然而止，展示了非传统结构的处理手法。整体而言，这是一张以北欧民谣素材为底色、带有实验性重构意图的作品，适合对斯堪的纳维亚民间音乐及其现代表达感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / soundscape / documentary
items._cn_summary: 这不是一张传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是声音工程师伊恩·布伦南在芝加哥枪支暴力幸存者社区进行的一次田野录音项目。录制地点位于一位94岁祖母家门前的前廊，靠近中途机场降落航道之下。25位年龄从17岁到67岁的参与者分享了各自被暴力影响的经历，部分人即兴说唱。编辑明确指出录音中未添加任何音乐，所有背景声均来自现场。参与者多为邻里居民，有人刚从追悼会赶来。发行收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方法终结暴力的组织。项目将芝加哥南区这一被遗忘区域的真实声音与社会议题结合，是田野录音与声音艺术介入社会现实的实践。

items.body: Review by Agnenrecords — Delirium's sixth studio album Sesta strada lungo il tempo (Sixth Road Through Time) was released in May this year, with a line-up similar to that responsible for 2015's L'Era della Menzogna, Enrico Tixi replacing drummer Alfredo Vandresi. It's not a concept album but references to the band's previous output, snapshots of time, characters and places, all create a series of linked stories embellished with a sense of Liguria and the sea.Opening with a multipart side-long track Schiavo della vilt� (Slave of Cowardice), it's obvious that the group are in full-on prog mode. The piece concerns itself with the morals of warfare through a protagonist who witnesses, and takes part in the horrors of war, knowing the acts are evil but is unable to speak out against them out of fear for what would happen to him. He reflects on leaving his lover behind as he sets off for war, and on the futility of conflict, the lives lost, never to dream, love or be free again. He finds his deeds shameful while his fellow soldiers seem to revel in the bloodshed in the name of the national flag. Musically, it fits together really well; different moods correspond to different sections and the lyrics, which recall Tremori antichi (from Lo scemo e il villaggio), are delivered with Corvaglia's dramatic vocals. Io clochard (I'm a Homeless Person) begins 'beyond the snow', blood-stained snow having featured in Schiavo della vilt�. A few bars of plaintive strings reflect the hardships of the protagonist; the dusty road and stale, mouldy bread that still tastes good, an indication that the perceived tribulations aren't unbearable. He's got his dog as a companion, time to rest and reflect, and a destination: the sea. The music primarily consists of a dense repeated phrase with a bubbly bass adding some colour, overlain with short saxophone breaks and a brief guitar solo, and guest vocalist Alice Vigo repeats the final verse in French.Il riposo del pirata (The Pirate's Rest) begins with ambient seashore sounds. Electric piano is employed in a rhythmic context, and saxophone and synthesizer weave around the vocal melody describing an old pirate in an old hammock, cradling a tankard of rum and listening to a song he can hear on the wind. Martial music indicates the final rest of the pirate and there'll be no more looting of treasure. The voices of the pirate crew can be discerned underneath Corvaglia's announcement, speaking in English: "I don't know what to do" and "I've had enough of this". Short organ sax and solos precede the final spoken verse, describing the crew celebrating the valour of the pirate on the sand where the waves bring in light foam reminiscent of freshly poured beer.Della strada il ritorno (On the Road Back) is a jazzy instrumental, beginning with string bass and piano. The piece has a real swing and there's a pleasing rhythmic complexity with Grice's saxophone soloing over the drums, bass and piano. A series of solos, energetic guitar, slower paced bass, flute, piano and sax complete the tune.Parole nel vento (Words in the Wind) has a fairly straightforward opening, before a flute riff, backed by hard rhythmic intervals, leads the song into Jethro Tull-like territory. I'm reminded of Corvaglia's track Il cerchio del comando on S.E.I. by La Maschera di Cera, which I've previously described as being like a Delirium song. Vigo shines on a lead synthesizer line that could have been performed by Keith Emerson, and following the last two vocal lines the band indulge in a blues blow out until the end of the song. While the lyrical content seems to reference both Il nome del vento ("The words thrown into the wind, who will listen?") and L'Era della Menzogna ("An ageless story made of a few lies and illusions mixed with fake freedom"), the track feels like it's pulling the strands of the four preceding stories together, creating a perfect ending.The whole album makes an enjoyable listen. It's well-crafted with a very high standard musicianship and production, expertly blending a distinct feel of past Delirium albums with an updated sound. Highly recommended.(This review originally appeared as part of a Delirium band history/album review on progblog.co.uk)
items._genre: rock progressivo italiano / symphonic prog / jazz-rock
items._cn_summary: 意大利摇滚乐队Delirium第六张录音室专辑《Sesta Strada Lungo il Tempo》以多重叙事串联碎片化的故事，主题围绕战争、漂泊与海洋，歌词带有浓郁的利古里亚地域色彩。开篇长篇作品《Schiavo della viltà》借战争亲历者的视角展开道德反思，《Io clochard》以萨克斯与低沉吟唱的弦乐刻画流浪者的苦乐参半，《Il riposo del pirata》引入海浪环境音与电钢琴描绘老海盗的终局。专辑在器乐上融合了萨克斯独奏、即兴段落与爵士化律动，器乐曲目《Della strada il ritorno》展现明显的爵士摇摆节奏与复合节奏编排，吉他与键盘交替推动段落发展。整体延续了乐队对意大利前卫摇滚传统的继承，同时在叙事结构和器乐编排上具有一定的纵深，但缺乏显著的实验性突破或电子化处理。

items.body: And all this time I’ve been hurting for you Whatever I tried, it didn’t matter And all of my heart has been aching for you Gave all of my love – did it even matter? There is something fitting about Jonny Pierce opening his new label Abysmal Records with a song about emotional nullification. The Drums have spent fifteen years turning romantic injury into bright, economical pop, yet It Didn’t Matter, a collaboration with Mareux, carries a colder sense of aftermath. Its title lands with the bluntness of a verdict delivered after the argument has ended, when language has been exhausted, and the abandoned person is left to rearrange the evidence. Mareux’s presence is immediately legible. Aryan Ashtiani supplies synthesizers that glide with severe elegance, placing Pierce’s voice inside a glassy architecture of drum-machine momentum and bruised pop chords straight off the 80s pop charts. The production remains clean without becoming sterile; each element has room to move, while the song’s forward motion suggests somebody walking quickly through a city to avoid calling the person they are trying to forget. Pierce sings with the fragile directness that has long defined The Drums, though age has added a finer grain to his delivery. Foolishness, need, and disbelief are presented without disguise. The song describes someone trapped in the aftermath of an unequal relationship, still longing for a partner who pushed them away without releasing them. Hurt, ashamed, and angry at themselves for needing love, they question whether their devotion, sacrifice, and enduring pain ever meant anything to the person they loved. Pierce describes the session in unusually personal terms: “Not since writing my earliest music has a song come together so effortlessly. Whenever that happens, it makes me feel certain the song was meant to exist -that it needed to be here, for all of us. Mareux’s synthesizer wizardry threw me back to my teenage years, when almost everything I listened to was synthesizer-based music, especially synth-pop. His sounds, textures, and perfect pop chord changes reminded me of the soundtrack to such a tender time in my life – when I was desperate for love but just couldn’t find it, and synthesizers became the soundtrack to my sadness. This one is for those of us who keep banging our heads against the wall of another heart, only to be given nothing in return.” The collaboration grants Mareux increasing space to move beyond the viral mythology of his Cure cover, “The Perfect Girl,” showcasing him as a composer whose precise synthesizer skills elevate another artist’s songwriting and emotion. A disciplined bassline, succinct percussion, and sighing keys anchor Pierce’s confession here, letting the melody carry the emotional weight that the production keeps in elegant balance. Watch the visualizer for It Didn’t Matter below: It Didn’t Matter‘s autobiographical charge belongs to a lineage of synth-pop where polished surfaces intensify private collapse, but Pierce and Ashtiani avoid empty period detail. Their shared instincts meet in the space between romantic candour and formal restraint, producing a track that feels immediate without sounding disposable. As the first entry in a six-month series of collaborations, it gives Abysmal Records a persuasive opening statement. More importantly, it suggests that Pierce’s next phase may be built through exchange rather than isolation. It Didn’t Matter turns rejection into motion, carrying its unanswered question forward with poise, clarity and a quietly devastating hook. Catch Mareux live this autumn: 09/19 — Santa Ana, CA — Observatory Festival Grounds with AFI, Kumo 99, and L.A. Witch 10/30 — London, UK — Hootananny Brixton 10/31 — Paris/Montreuil, France — Bal Chavaux 11/03 — Athens, Greece — Floyd Live Music Venue 11/05 — Istanbul, Turkey — IF Performance Hall Beşiktaş 11/07 — Tbilisi, Georgia — Academy Follow The Drums: Instagram Spotify Follow Mareux: Website Instagram YouTube Facebook TikTok Bandcamp The post “All This Time I’ve Been Hurting for You” — Mareux and The Drums Collaborate on New Single “It Didn’t Matter” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: The Drums 主唱 Jonny Pierce 联合暗潮电子制作人 Mareux 发布合作单曲，作为其新厂牌 Abysmal Records 的开篇之作。歌曲以冷调的合成器架构和鼓机节奏构建 80 年代 synth-pop 质感，Pierce 的声线在锐利的键盘铺陈中呈现脆弱而直接的情感表达。歌词围绕一段不平等关系结束后的内心废墟展开——长期的付出与牺牲在对方眼中是否毫无意义。制作上 Mareux 的合成器编排被精准定位，以克制的低音线、简洁的打击乐和叹息般的键盘和弦支撑主唱的忏诉式旋律，展现其超越病毒式翻唱之外的作曲能力。整体氛围延续了合成器流行乐中以光亮表面承载私密崩溃的传统脉络，对暗潮与后朋克听众有一定吸引力，但在实验性与声音创新方面偏保守。

items.body: Machine Command, an EBM project, released the single “Rage” on August 4, 2026. The single follows the 2026 album “Cathected” and is available on Bandcamp and Spotify. Rage by Machine Command “Rage” holds two versions of the track. The main version runs at 145 BPM as an EBM stomper, with a vocal delivery the band describes as somewhere between Rein and Anne Clarke. The second version, titled “Rage (Vocoder Dub Mix)”, uses vocodered vocals over an electrofunk arrangement the band compares to Cabaret Voltaire. Lyrically, the song addresses how social media places people into echo chambers and sets them against each other. “Rage” is the first single from a new Machine Command album, scheduled for release sometime in 2027. Machine Command describes its sound as appealing to fans of Nitzer Ebb and Portion Control, as well as newer acts such as Ultra Sunn and Ruined Conflict. On August 28, 2026, Machine Command supports Rotersand at The Helling in Utrecht, Netherlands. Additional shows are in preparation. About Machine Command Machine Command is an EBM project of Pieter Winkelaar and Annemarie Janssen. The project’s Bandcamp discography includes the albums “4PM”, “Deformed”, “Strength”, “To The Point”, “New Socialism”, “Stampfbereit”, “Two Point Zero”, “Decline and Rise Again”, “Nuke It from Orbit” and “Cathected”, the latter released March 11, 2026, alongside the EPs “Tetrarchy E.P.” and “Without Fear EP” and additional singles and remix releases. Side-Line previously covered the band’s “Affected” album. “Rage” continues that release chronology and adds the Rotersand support date to the project’s upcoming live schedule.
items._cn_summary: Machine Command 是一支以电子身体音乐为核心的二人计划，新单曲《Rage》包含两个版本。主版本以 145 BPM 的节奏推进，人声处理被描述为介于 Rein 与 Anne Clarke 之间，硬朗且具有辨识度；Vocoder Dub Mix 版本则转向 electrofunk 编排，灵感来源于 Cabaret Voltaire。歌词层面，作品聚焦社交媒体如何将人们困于信息回音室并使其互相敌对这一社会议题。乐队自称面向 Nitzer Ebb、Portion Control 等经典工业/电子听众，同时也吸引 Ultra Sunn、Ruined Conflict 等新一代暗潮群体。该单曲是计划于 2027 年发行的新专辑首支先行曲，乐队的 discography 涵盖十张全长专辑与若干 EP，作品体系扎实。整体而言，这是一篇偏新闻稿性质的发布通告，缺乏深度评论与听觉分析，但所涉风格属于用户关注范畴内的常规工业电子作品。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Breathless' is Camel's sixth album and the band's last one with original keyboard player PeterBardens as well as their second and final release to feature Richard Sinclair of Caravan. Thisrecord is a logical continuation of the stylistic evolution of the band's previous albums (startingwith 'Moonmadness' and going through 'Rain Dances'), with Camel exploring a rather accessiblevariation of their melodic style of progressive rock. Scant jazzy interludes can still be heard onthis album, although Mel Collins' presence and impact are virtually non-existent. 'Breathless' mightvery well be classified as an art pop record with proggy arrangements, on which the vocals are asunimpressive as usual.By the way, the vocal duties on this album are divided equally between R. Sinclair, who isundeniably the more capable singer, and Andy Latimer, whose limited range works well within thecontext of Camel's mellow (and at times soporific) music. Some of the better songs featured on thisalbum include the title track, which is a sappy art pop number, the much more sophisticated 'Echoes'with its ornate instrumentals and sheltering melodies as well as the 7-minute track 'The Sleeper', asong exhibiting a fancy Canetrbury-esque nuance in the keyboards. 'Summer Lightning' surprises as anice example of danceable prog, while the rest is tame and dreamy, and perhaps not everybody's cupof tea. The album as a whole is decent and enjoyable, but parts of it are truly boring andunremarkable.
items._genre: symphonic prog / art pop / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Camel乐队1978年的第六张专辑，也是键盘手Peter Bardens在队期间的最后一张作品。专辑延续了乐队自《Moonmadness》以来的渐进演变，呈现出更易接近的旋律性前卫摇滚风格。制作上融入了少量爵士过渡段落，键盘与吉他交织出装饰性的器乐段落。主唱任务由Richard Sinclair和Andy Latimer平分，前者演唱能力更佳，后者有限的音域反倒契合乐队慵懒朦胧的音乐气质。代表作包括同名曲这种带有艺术流行色彩的曲目，《Echoes》以华丽器乐与庇护性旋律见长，《The Sleeper》则展现出坎特伯雷式的键盘处理，《Summer Lightning》意外地带出可舞动的节奏感。整体制作规整，旋律流畅，但部分段落显得平淡乏味，缺乏真正的突破性元素。

items.body: Band: beauty is the end | Album: White Knuckle Dress | Genre: Art rock, Progressive pop | Bandcamp Ever wonder what Spock’s Beard might sound like if they were a lightly-folky art-pop band? Well, I think beauty is the end is a pretty good approximation of that idea. Their songs are long and complexly-structured, with some flashy and emotive instrumentalism. Tones are mostly bright, but they also ably deploy tense, minor-key moments well. I really enjoy how prominent violin is throughout the record, and melodies are pretty consistently catchy. Certain passages are a bit cheesier than I’d normally go for, but this record is an overall success. The 10-minute “Domesticated” is a definite highlight. Score: 76/100 Band: Brass Camel | Album: Brass Camel | Genre: Progressive rock | Bandcamp Brass Camel’s third album is a peppy, punchy, enthusiastic, and unashamedly retro-sounding record. They lean heavily into classic rock, hard rock, and glam rock tropes and imbue it with Yes-like technical flashiness. They remind me a lot of acts like (early) Kansas or some of Queen’s more ambitious moments. The sound is maximal and bright, and they effortlessly weave catchy pop melodies alongside complex instrumental displays. I wouldn’t call this an essential release, but it’s a lot of fun, and it’s an example of how to do proggy retro-rock well. Score: 75/100 Artist: Me El-Ma | Album: Forward Owner | Genre: Progressive rock | Bandcamp The newest solo album from Israeli drummer and composer Me El-Ma demonstrates a lot of ambition and some stellar performances. The music is complex and diverse, drawing from classic prog, avant-garde influences, folk, classical, and Levantine music. Unfortunately, this can frequently result in a lot of songs coming off as muddled, unfocused, and complicated for complication’s sake. The vocals are also strikingly similar to those of Jon Anderson, and the credit being given to “VIRJA” makes me think they may be artificially-generated. (I’m guessing VIRJA stands for something like Virtual Intelligent Recreation of Jon Anderson.) And I wonder if Jon Anderson gave his okay for his voice to be used like this. (I’m also fairly confident that the guitars are programmed, but I have no real issue with that, as El-Ma says all this was written by him.) Score: 53/100 Band: Korbo | Album: Amnésiste | Genre: Progressive rock | Bandcamp This French quartet plays an energetic, relatively heavy variety of progressive rock. Their sound is impactful and powerful, drawing from classic hard rock, punk, and metal. Occasional jazzy licks serve as nice points of contrast. “Chaînes” sees the band dip into some mild doom and sludge flavors, though parts of this particular cut can feel a bit dragged-out. In general, though, despite the long runtimes, most of the songs feel well-structured. Score: 74/100 Band: Osees | Album: Cara Maluco EP | Genre: Krautrock, Psychedelic rock | Bandcamp Ever-prolific psych-punks Osees are back with a new EP of wiry psychedelia. Elements of punk, post-punk, and noise rock are prominent here. This is Osees at a moment when they’ve shifted their focus back to guitar-based music, in contrast to their frequent synth excursions. The sprawling title track is energetic and fun, if a bit unfocused, and I love the twangy tones of “Joro”. “Synaptic Static” is bright and sunny, but it feels a little underbaked. The closing “Joy in Oblivion” is the weirdest and wildest cut on this release, despite clocking in at under two minutes, and it’s probably my favorite here. Score: 73/100 Band: Tortue | Album: Mëändyou | Genre: Zeuhl, Progressive electronic | Bandcamp This one-man act from St. Louis presents a completely unexpected but deeply enjoyable vision for zeuhl on this album. The album title is taken from The Turtles’ “Happy Together”, vocal samples from which play a prominent role on this album. In addition to Magmatic repetition and jazzy instrumental tones, high-energy electronica (which I think might be classifiable as drum-and-bass; I’m not 100%, as I’m hardly an expert) keeps this sonic experiment zipping along. This 40-minute, four-part suite has moments of both great intensity with maximal arrangements and more restrained passages that often cultivate dread. My one real gripe about Mëändyou is its length. There are a lot of cool ideas, but parts of this record can feel a bit on the needlessly-drawn-out side of things, even by the standards of a repetition-loving genre like zeuhl. Score: 70/100
items._genre: progressive rock / art rock / progressive pop / psychedelic rock / krautrock
items._cn_summary: 本期合集涵盖五组艺术摇滚与前卫摇滚方向的新作。beauty is the end 以明亮音色与复杂结构著称，小提琴贯穿全辑，旋律抓耳，在 Spock's Beard 式技巧与民谣艺术流行之间取得平衡。Brass Camel 的同名专辑走复古路线，融合经典摇滚、华丽摇滚与 Yes 式炫技段落，最大化编制下兼顾流行旋律与复杂器乐。Me El-Ma 的《Forward Owner》由以色列鼓手创作，跨越前卫摇滚、古典、犹太与中东音乐素材，但部分曲目结构显得散乱且过度复杂，人声疑似使用 AI 模拟 Jon Anderson 的音色。法国乐队 Korbo 演奏硬朗而富有冲击力的前卫摇滚，融入硬摇滚、朋克与金属元素，偶有爵士调味。Osees 发布短篇 EP，以瘦削的迷幻摇滚与德国泡菜摇滚为基调，维持高产创作节奏。整体而言，这些作品多数落在传统前卫摇滚谱系内，融合元素丰富但实验性有限。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)
items.label: Buda Musique
items._genre: bal-musette / ragtime / French chanson / jug band / eclectic fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominique Cravic与未来原始人乐队的第五张录音，由地下漫画家Robert Crumb绘制封面。音乐风格被描述为难以归类，乐器涵盖手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等27首短曲。内容融合了法国手风琴舞曲、拉格泰姆、Jug乐队、法国香颂乃至skiffle等元素，跨越1920年代至当代的曲目，既有幽默的尤克里里老歌，也有向法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的作品。Cravic以类似Maurice Chevalier的念白式唱腔演绎，乐手多为七旬老人，以严肃态度与热情复活被遗忘的旧日风格，评论将其与Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks相提并论。

items.body:
LOCAL（国内）
NEWS
10/03~10 小橋敦子＆トニー・オーヴァーウォーター
Japan Tour 2026 PORGY ALIVE
2026年8月4日
編集部

アムステルダムを本拠地に活動を展開するピアノの小橋敦子とコントラバスのトニー・オーヴァーウォーターのデュオが10月早々に日本ツアーを予定している。
ジョン・コルトレーンの楽曲を中心にした2021年のアルバム『Crescent』がオランダの最高峰の音楽賞であるエジソン大賞およびドイツのレコード批評家大賞のジャズ部門にノミネートされ一躍高い評価を得たあと、ドラマーが手がけた名曲を取り上げた『A Drum Thing』（2023年）、ジョージ・ガーシュウィンの『ポーギーとベス』を独自の視点で再解釈した作品『Porgy』（2025年）を通じてデュオとして確固たる地歩を築いた。とくに、守破離（Shu-Ha-Ri）の哲学にインスパイアされた『Porgy』は対話を軸に「静寂とダイナミクス」「東洋と西洋の感性の融合」の具現化に成功、国際的な評価を得てカイロ・ジャズ・フェスやノース・シー・ジャズ・フェスへの出演をもたらした。
今回のツアーでは彼らの高音質なアルバムに通じる会場が厳選されている点にも注目したい。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Mental Architects are a very interesting math rock band from Bulgaria, that is unfortunately nolonger active. The trio consisting of Tony Velev (guitars), Nikki Ranguelov (bass), and MaxStoimenov (drums) tackles a rhythmically complex style that is simultaneously melodic, light-hearted, and digestible. Unlike many contemporary names in the math rock scene, MA have the peculiartendency to write fun and catchy sophisticated music, as you will often hear neat riffs and grooved-out chords on their 2012 studio album 'Celebrations', which is officially their third outing. Thereis an ostensible yet subtle post-rock aftertaste all over this record, but definitely not in theform of otherworldly crescendos or extended solos. The album is pretty playful and energetic, and tomy ears, one of the few math rock collections that could make you want to... dance?Why not; after all this is a celebratory album that impresses with a vast and flourishing guitarsound, often enough relying on multiple lines working around each other (this is a strong studioproject, above all), while the bass guitar and the drums, as tasty as they are, remain lessprominent, or even a little restrained, if you will. Had the band been more fusion-oriented, therhythm section could have been more unconventional and more prone to experimentation, but MentalArchitects' music is incredibly enjoyable, nonetheless. The compositions that certainly impress meon this album are 'Spell Shelter', 'Here Is Where, Where Better' (respectively the first and secondtracks), the 7-minute-long 'Ace of Keys', which is mesmerizing, and the song called 'Meth-Rock',which appears towards the end of the album. There is a joyous warmth to the music on 'Celebrations',which will appeal to many listeners, but that album cover... it's just alright.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由保加利亚三人乐队Mental Architects创作，是一张节奏复杂却旋律轻快、朗朗上口的数学摇滚作品。吉他作为核心乐器，多条旋律线交织穿梭，构建出广阔而丰富的吉他音色层次。贝斯与鼓机能在其中保持了恰到好处的克制，为整体提供了稳定的节奏骨架。整张专辑氛围欢快活泼，散发着庆祝般的温暖感，在数学摇滚类型中相对易听且具有舞曲律动感，同时带有微妙的后摇滚余韵。专辑推荐曲目包括开篇的《Spell Shelter》和《Here Is Where, Where Better》、长达七分钟的迷人之作《Ace of Keys》，以及接近尾声的《Meth-Rock》。评论特别提到专辑封面设计平平，但对于乐队作品的音乐性给予了肯定。整体而言，这是一张偏向类型内部的精雕细琢之作，融合了数学摇滚的复杂节奏与后摇滚的氛围感。

items.body: Review by ken_scrbrgh — There is an irony that I am considering Steve Howe's, "Beginnings," after ruminating over the four other Yes' solo albums released in 1975-1976: Howe's was the first to make its premiere. "Authentic" is the adjective I would like to employ in pondering this album almost fifty-one years after its emergence."Yesfreak" that I was back then and now, I must admit that, unlike Chris Squire's, "Fish Out of Water," I was not drawn to "Beginnings." In truth, for many years, I was seriously familiar only with Squire's album. Only since 2023, have I thoroughly come to appreciate Anderson, White, and Moraz' efforts. I would venture Howe's record emerged first in 1975 as the result of the solo work he maintained parallel to his work with Yes. I have to speculate that during the conception and initial execution of the pieces destined to yield "Beginnings," Howe chose to sing the lead vocals. Perhaps, then, as a matter of economy and facilitation, he opted to retain his lead vocal performances? If we consider 2023's, "Mirror to the Sky" and this year's, "Aurora," we encounter "successful" lead vocals from Howe on, "Unknown Place" and "Countermovement." Surely, though, in the mid-Seventies, Howe's lead vocals on his first solo album attenuated attention given to this effort.Then and now this lack of interest is unfortunate. As a generalization, "Beginnings'" compositions, instrumentality, and lyrics are effective; the poem "Doors of Sleep" by Alice Meynell sets the stage for the entire album. On "Doors of Sleep" and "Lost Symphony," the vocals are fine. With White at the drums, Howe performs all other instruments on the album opener. Perhaps the direct means of appreciating Howe's first album lies in the instrumentals "Beginnings" and "Nature of the Sea." With orchestration by Patrick Moraz, "Beginnings" certainly draws upon the "symphonic" in "prog." I would also add "chamber" and "neo-Baroque." One might consider "Beginnings" to be Howe's "answer" to the chamber orchestra on "Time and a Word." Through this piece, Howe displays his studied approach to classical guitar and to the use of the volume pedal. Although not orchestral, "The Nature of the Sea," gives us further insight into the compositional character of Steve Howe's imagination in the mid-Seventies. With an ensemble of players found only on this album's song (Malcolm Bennett, bass, David Oberle, drums, and Graeme Taylor, guitar), Howe exemplifies the "ebb and flow" of an ocean, rendering a microcosm of "Tales from the Topographic Oceans."Considering "Will 'O' The Wisp," one can visualize Howe, Moraz, and White in the studio contemporaneously with "Relayer" or shortly thereafter. With Moraz' mellotron, Howe parallels the ephemeral character of love's relationships with the paranormal, "Will 'O' The Wisp."Perhaps "Lost Symphony" is the truly solid, single piece on "Beginnings." Here, we venture into jazz with the saxophone and productive lead vocals by Howe. As with "Will 'O' The Wisp," Moraz and White support."Beginnings" provides us with an authentic window into the creative mind of Steve Howe in the mid-Seventies. For those of us who have been given the "gift of time," we can perceive the origins of the narrative of Howe's musical journey.
items._genre: Crossover Prog / symphonic rock / chamber prog
items._cn_summary: 这是Yes吉他手Steve Howe 1975年的首张个人专辑。评论者将其置于Yes成员同时期几张个人作品的语境中比较，认为专辑内含古典吉他、室内乐和新巴洛克等元素，编曲由Patrick Moraz参与管弦化处理。整张专辑 Howe 几乎包揽了所有乐器演奏，少数曲目由Alan White或临时乐手客座。专辑以Alice Meynell的诗作《Doors of Sleep》开场，器乐曲如《Beginnings》和《Nature of the Sea》展示了作者对古典吉他与音量踏板的运用；后者的编制可视为《Tales from Topographic Oceans》海洋意象的微缩呈现。另一些曲目带有爵士色彩，如加入萨克斯的《Lost Symphony》。评论者认为 Howe 当时的嗓音是这张专辑未能获得广泛关注的因素之一，但从作曲、器乐演奏与歌词层面来看，作品本身具有扎实的完成度。

items.body: Review by Atri Isla — Images and Words is my‑favorite album. On this record, Dream Theater perfectly blends progressive ideas with heartfelt emotional expression. The instrumental arrangements are intricate yet full of beauty. Pull Me Under is a progressive‑metal track with pop‑oriented qualities. I am deeply impressed by the atmosphere built within its intro.Another Day delivers magnificent emotional expression, and its solo is absolutely breathtaking.Metropolis Pt.1 "The Miracle and the Sleeper" is a brilliant narrative piece. It lays out the outline and key hints for the whole Metropolis story, which later inspired the creation of Metropolis Pt. 2.The closing track Learning to Live, in my opinion, is the most underrated song on the album. James LaBrie's vocal performance here is simply stunning.To sum up, Images and Words pioneered a brand‑new creative paradigm for progressive metal and marks the starting‑point of modern progressive metal. Its power of emotional expression stands nearly unrivaled among works of this genre.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑被作者视为Dream Theater的代表作，将前卫摇滚的复杂结构与金属乐的力度相结合，同时融入流行音乐的可听性。器乐编排精细繁复，吉他独奏段落展现高度技术性，人声演唱情感饱满。从结构上看，专辑通过叙事性的长篇作品串联整体概念，为后续作品埋下伏笔。情感表达被作者认为在同类作品中具有标杆意义。然而，专辑整体仍属传统的前卫金属范畴，在实验性元素、声音设计或跨界融合方面着墨有限，与前卫实验、爵士即兴或电子音乐等领域的探索存在明显距离。评论内容较为简略，缺乏对具体音色处理或编曲细节的深入剖析。

items.body: German electronic pop project Arsine Tibé and vocalist Suzanne Letting release the four-track concept mini-album “Reclaimed” on August 7, 2026. The digital release is a collaboration between Arsine Tibé, the solo project of Manfred Thomaser, and Letting, and centers on the experience of a woman who has survived violence, told in the first person. Thomaser describes the record’s subject as a widespread problem: “Violence against women and girls is one of the most widespread and common human rights violations worldwide.” He adds that the first-person narrative structure was chosen deliberately, to create “an immediate – and therefore very emotional – connection to the subject.” The mini-album’s main track is “Ghost Doorway”. Its official video goes online on August 7 at midnight CET, on the same day as the digital release. Arsine Tibé and Letting are also preparing a CD and vinyl edition of “Reclaimed” that will additionally include instrumental versions of all four songs; no release date for the physical formats has been confirmed yet. ‘Reclaimed’ ties into a Refuge fundraiser Arsine Tibé and Letting will donate proceeds from the CD and vinyl sales of “Reclaimed” to Refuge, the UK’s largest specialist domestic abuse organisation. Letting has separately set up a fundraising page for Refuge on JustGiving to support the same cause. About Arsine Tibé Arsine Tibé is the Lounge Noire and electronic pop solo project of Manfred Thomaser, based in Munich, Germany. Thomaser describes the project’s sound as drawing on lounge, soundtrack, ambient, new wave, electro and pop elements. He is best known as one half of !Distain, the German synthpop duo he shares with Alexander Braun, and has also worked on the projects Demokratie and The Independent Seasons. Side-Line first covered Arsine Tibé in February 2016, when Thomaser launched a mini-album under the project name, led by the track “Obligation”. Arsine Tibé has since released several collaborations with Suzanne Letting, including “Beyond the Point (feat. Suzanne Letting)” and the two-part The Lounge Noire Sessions, the second episode of which appeared on June 19, 2026. “Reclaimed” continues that collaboration and marks the pair’s first release built around a dedicated social theme, with its charity tie-in to Refuge.
items._cn_summary: 德国电子音乐人Arsine Tibé与歌手Suzanne Letting合作发行的四曲概念迷你专辑，以第一人称叙事方式讲述女性暴力幸存者的经历，主题严肃且具有社会关怀。音乐风格融合lounge、new wave、ambient、electro与流行元素，介于合成器流行与暗潮之间。专辑包含器乐版本，实体发行收益将捐给英国反家暴慈善机构Refuge。制作人Thomaser此前以合成器二人组!Distain闻名，此次作品延续了与Letting的合作脉络，但风格上更偏向氛围化的电子流行，而非深度实验。整体属于独立小厂牌发行的小众欧洲电子项目，主题立意值得肯定，但在声音创新性和前卫性上较为温和。

items.body: Princess Ugly, a post-punk and darkwave act, released the single “The Work” on August 4, 2026, together with a remix by Leæther Strip’s Claus Larsen. Both versions are available on Bandcamp, YouTube and other streaming platforms. The Work by Princess Ugly Lyrically, “The Work” presents what the band describes as an existential, ontological horror built on EBM-influenced instrumentation, addressing a compulsion to work and create that ultimately turns the created thing into something that stalks and controls its maker. The official video for “The Work” is embedded below. The single is accompanied by a remix from Leæther Strip‘s Claus Larsen. Princess Ugly describes the “Leæther Strip Remix” as a dense, infectious reinterpretation with a biting electro-industrial groove. The remix is also on Bandcamp and has its own video. About Princess Ugly Princess Ugly are J. Christopher-Rome (words, vocals) and Christopher Moncrieffe (music, instruments), based in Portland, Oregon. The project began as a solo effort from J. Christopher-Rome with a first album released in 2006; Christopher Moncrieffe joined in 2007, and the pair released two albums as a duo, “The Past, One Second At A Time” (2010) and “It Should Be Clear By Now” (2012). After a hiatus, Princess Ugly returned in 2021 with a run of singles and EPs that leaned further into post-punk and goth influences, starting with “Hunger” (2021) and continuing through “Start Below” (2022), “An Individual Soul” (2023), “Break Every Room” (2023), the EP “Death After Life” (2023), the EP “Bring the Axes” (2024) and the single “The Out” (2025). The band also appeared on the Belgian label Spleen+’s post-punk box set “Resurgence” (2025). “The Work” and its Leæther Strip remix follow that run of singles and mark the band’s latest release.

Christopher-Rome 与 Christopher Moncrieffe 组成，来自波特兰，自 2006 年起以双人编制活跃至今，并简要回顾了自 2021 年回归以来的单曲与 EP 发行脉络。原创版本以 EBM 影响的器乐为基础，构建关于工作与创作执念的存在主义恐怖主题；Leæther Strip 的混音版则被描述为密集、具有感染力的电波工业再造，带有尖锐的咬合感。两版均已在 Bandcamp、YouTube 及主流流媒体平台同步上线。作为信息发布，内容完整但缺乏深度音乐分析与艺术性评价。

items.body:
Jazz's most exciting duo are making their way back to Thailand. DOMi & JD BECK are set to return to Bangkok for DOMi & JD BECK WHO ASKED? Tour Live in Bangkok 2026 on 24 November at Sphere Hall, EMSPHERE, marking the duo's first performance in the city since their sold-out debut nearly two years ago.

Comprised of keyboardist Domi Louna and drummer JD Beck, the GRAMMY-nominated pair have earned a reputation for pushing the boundaries of contemporary jazz through their fearless blend of virtuosic musicianship, intricate rhythms, and playful experimentation. Their acclaimed debut album, NOT TiGHT, garnered two GRAMMY nominations, including Best New Artist, while standout performances on NPR Tiny Desk, Jimmy Kimmel Live, and The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon introduced their genre-defying sound to audiences around the world.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by VIJICORP (@vijicorp)

Their Bangkok return arrives in support of their sophomore album, WHO ASKED?, which was released on 31 July via Anderson .Paak's APESHIT label in partnership with Blue Note Records. The new record continues the duo's adventurous musical journey, weaving together shifting time signatures, electronic textures, and improvisational flair into a sound that's uniquely their own.

Following a memorable sold-out performance in Thailand, DOMi & JD BECK are set to reunite with Thai fans for another night of unpredictable performances and boundary-pushing musicianship. The upcoming show promises to showcase the next chapter of the duo's evolving catalogue while celebrating the chemistry that has made them one of the most exciting acts in modern jazz.

Ticket details:

Tickets on sale: 7 August, 10 AM (Bangkok time)

Ticketing: www.ticketmelon.com/vjela/domijdbeck2026

items.body: Review by alainPP — SYRINX CALL operates outside of time, with flutes galore exuding a strong folk vibe; Mirrorneuron is an empathy-dispensing AI controlled by Mara?an intricate psychotherapist figure in this supernatural fable that echoes the style of SINGLE CELLED ORGANISM.'Returning' kicks off with a SINGLE CELLED ORGANISM feel?fitting, given the flute that defines the band's signature atmosphere. It's modern progressive rock?layered and ethereal?flowing into'Boundless Choices,' where Kate Bush and Pink Floyd hover in the background alongside warm vocals; a blend of prog and neo-classical styles featuring swirling guitars and an enchanting flute.'Organic Embodiment' carries hints of ANGE in its melody, while Hannes's heavy build-up evokes ELOY. Jens's velvety vocals briefly recall the soaring heights of SYLVAN or classic-era MARILLION. The whole track is sprinkled with flute and female vocalizations.'Are You My Image' features female vocals and an ambient folk-pop sound reminiscent of ENYA or IONA?truly magical; the guitar arpeggios and flute create a moment of simple, ineffable beauty.'Wheels of Emotion' follows, with narration set against the flute, leading to an emotional breakdown featuring a guitar solo that appears out of nowhere?a solemn moment touching greatness, with sharp guitar work reminiscent of MARILLION. The flute-driven folk drift shares this medieval-troubadour-style track with a big 80s-style keyboard solo and a dash of *Different Light*-era vibes.'Yearning' continues the conceptual journey, with the AI ​​narrating the atmospheric space setting. It is a long, building track?saccharine-sweet in its vocals, yet solid and substantial in its instrumentation. The finale, featuring Isgaard's spellbinding vocals, is truly outstanding. "Attachment," featuring Doris, offers a pastoral ballad reminiscent of days gone by?think JADIS or ELOY?showcasing languid six-string work that flirts with a Floydian atmosphere. The keyboards strongly evoke ELOY?delivering that weighty sound perfect for navigating the landscape of German progressive rock?followed by another Floydian outro featuring waves of sound."Emptiness" follows, led by the alto flute for a gentle, melancholic interlude; Isgaard once again takes center stage with an elven vocal performance over a crystalline piano finale."Mind Over Matter" comes next, blending flute and piano into another melting folk-prog excursion, with Jens's keyboard touches guiding the listener toward a heroic fantasy realm; it is an ethereal ballad that eventually crashes into..."Here..." an interlude defined by its dark alto flute?a moment of suspended anticipation."...And Now" brings back the energy with a soft-heavy riff and reverb-laden guitar, recalling the New Age sounds of APSARAS. The melody begins to circle back on itself slightly, though one must acknowledge that sustaining an hour of such high quality is no small feat. It is time to leave; cinematic footsteps sound before Isgaard calls us to..."The Difference," a track redolent of Kate Bush; the epilogue to a musical odyssey, complete with laughter, tears, doubt, and hope.SYRINX CALL has released a musical gem that builds upon the foundation of their previous album. It is a slow musical journey where the tracks weave a spell, causing you to lose yourself and fall under their hypnotic influence. The sound is an energetic and glamorous blend of folk, rock, and prog?sharp, effective, and polished. (4.75)
